title: Bosch Illustration Style - Brand Guide and Digital Design System Research
intent: Structured extraction of research findings about how Bosch illustration style is defined, governed, and applied through the Bosch Brand Guide and Bosch Digital Design System, with emphasis on digital touchpoints.
recommended_audiences: teams creating Bosch-compliant digital or communication visuals

covered_topics: Relationship between Brand Guide and BDDS
scope.primary_focus: How illustration style is defined by the Bosch Brand Guide and applied to digital touchpoints through BDDS.
excluded_topics: Full visual inventory of every illustration asset
Final prompt templates for image generation
Legal approval process beyond high-level AI-image-generation constraints
scope.ambiguity_policy: If a source did not explicitly state a rule, the research records the point as an inference or ambiguity rather than treating it as binding guidance.

executive_summary.short_definition: Bosch illustration style is a centrally governed corporate design style defined in the Bosch Brand Guide and applied across media, including digital touchpoints through BDDS. It is characterized by clear, modern, flat 2.5D geometric illustrations, controlled use of Bosch brand colors, gray gradations, reduced detail, and a strong focus on comprehension.
executive_summary.main_conclusion: The Bosch Brand Guide is the root authority for illustration style. BDDS does not create a separate illustration language; it translates and operationalizes Brand Guide principles for digital products, UI workflows, and implementation contexts.
practical_reading: For any Bosch illustration, start from the Brand Guide, Illustration Library, and Illustration Creator before creating something new.
For digital products, use BDDS and its associated design-development ecosystem to apply the same brand illustration style in UI contexts.
Custom or externally sourced illustrations are risky unless they strictly follow Bosch illustration rules and are reviewed through the appropriate design support path.
AI-generated illustrations should be treated as newly created design assets and therefore must follow Bosch style, legal, accessibility, and governance constraints.

core_style.description: Bosch illustration style is clear, modern, flat, and 2.5D. It uses modular, editable construction-kit logic so illustrations can be assembled and adapted across formats and media.

rules: Use basic geometric shapes as the construction basis.
Use clear edges and soft curves.
Build objects from simplified forms rather than detailed naturalistic drawing.
The shape language is inspired by Bosch symbol/logotype and typography.
geometry.intent: Create recognition, clarity, and consistency while avoiding overly expressive or arbitrary illustration styles.

rules: Use flat-design construction with controlled 2.5D spatial suggestion.
Depth can be created through layered composition, foreground/middle-ground/background structure, and gray gradations.
Avoid photorealistic 3D rendering, glossy effects, reflections, gradients, or heavy shadow effects.
depth_and_2_5d.interpretation: 2.5D means the illustration can imply spatial depth but should not become realistic 3D artwork.

rules: Use Bosch brand colors only.
Design each illustration within a color scheme.
Use color selectively to draw attention to the most important element.
Use gray gradations for secondary and supporting elements.
Subtly tint gradations according to the chosen color scheme where needed.
Avoid too many colors and avoid non-Bosch-specific colors.
Avoid gradients and special visual effects.
theme_support: Light theme illustrations can appear on white backgrounds.
Dark theme illustrations can appear on dark backgrounds.
Light and dark theme usage should preserve contrast and readability.

rules: Place the most important element in the center foreground.
Use supporting elements in the middle ground to clarify context.
Use reduced background elements to add subtle depth and stage the action.
Reduce the environment so it supports the message without distracting from the main subject.
Assemble people, objects, and environments into a final motif that tells one clear story.
Represent people with simple and organic body forms.
Vary clothing, hairstyle, and accessories to create different figures.
Show diversity without using classic naturalistic skin colors.
Use brand colors from the selected color scheme or gray palette for people.
Avoid overly realistic facial or anatomical details.
people_representation.purpose: Support inclusive and flexible representation while preserving Bosch's abstract and modular visual language.

rules: Objects should support the visual story rather than dominate unnecessarily.
Objects may be developed from Bosch icon forms as a starting point.
Object illustrations can add colors and details to icon-derived forms while preserving Bosch geometry.
Bosch icons may be integrated into illustrations when describing products or functions.
Icons should be color-matched to the illustration style.
Icons should be combined with supporting elements so they do not get lost in the scene.
Use Bosch Icon Library as the source for icon forms.
Illustrations can be animated.
People illustrations are designed so limbs can be animated individually.
Animation should preserve the Bosch illustration style and modular form logic.
animation.available_asset_reference: Bosch-Illustrations-Body-Parts-for-animation.zip was identified as an available animation support asset in the Brand Guide page.

dos: Focus on one primary color or one color scheme.
Use shades of gray for secondary elements.
Use approved Bosch Illustration Library assets when possible.
Use Illustration Creator when adapting or composing new visuals.
Use Bosch icons if icons are integrated into illustrations.
Keep the illustration comprehensible, vivid, and focused on one message.
donts: Do not use shadow-heavy visual effects.
Do not use too many colors.
Do not use arbitrary organic or highly detailed forms as the main visual language.
Do not use generic stock illustrations.
Do not purchase external icons or illustrations from image databases when Bosch libraries already provide compliant assets.
Do not create digital illustrations that visually diverge from the Brand Guide unless an approved exception exists.
risk_flags_for_review: Illustration contains gradients or glossy rendering.
Illustration uses photorealistic or generic 3D visualization.
Illustration includes unclear or unreadable UI text embedded inside the image.
Illustration is being used in a public or high-visibility Bosch touchpoint without design review.

execution_path: Search Illustration Library for released assets.
Use Illustration Creator if adaptation is needed.
Request Design Support review when creating new or high-visibility assets.

digital_product_context.primary_authority: BDDS for digital placement and UI behavior, Brand Guide for visual illustration style.
execution_path: Use BDDS for UI layout, spacing, color tokens, typography, components, and accessibility.
Use Brand Guide illustration rules for the illustration itself.
Prefer official illustration and icon libraries over custom assets.
Ensure digital accessibility such as sufficient contrast, alternative text, and no critical text trapped only in images.

brand_vs_digital_contexts.main_difference: Marketing contexts may use illustrations as key visuals, while digital product contexts usually use illustrations as supporting explanatory or state-based elements. The style remains consistent in both contexts.
brand_vs_digital_contexts.main_consistency_rule: Regardless of channel, the illustration must remain Bosch-compliant: flat, geometric, 2.5D, brand-color controlled, reduced, and purposeful.

accessibility_rules: Illustrations in digital contexts should not contain essential text that is unavailable to assistive technologies.
Provide alternative text or equivalent description when illustrations communicate meaningful information.
Maintain sufficient contrast in light and dark theme applications.
Use BDDS color and accessibility rules for digital placement.
ai_image_generation_rules: For AI-generated images, use only Bosch-approved tools where required by internal guidance.
Follow internal legal AI guidance and copyright rules.
Consult the responsible legal or design authority before using unapproved AI image tools for Bosch assets.
Treat AI-generated illustrations as newly created design assets requiring Bosch style compliance and review.
external_assets_policy: Avoid buying external icons or illustrations because Bosch already provides compliant libraries.
External stock images may be relevant for imagery, but stock illustrations and icons should not replace Bosch-approved illustration and icon libraries.

why_this_research_matters_for_ai: The Bosch illustration style can be encoded as machine-readable constraints for AI image generation and design review.
The rules are specific enough to guide prompts: flat 2.5D, geometric shapes, one color scheme, gray secondary elements, no gradients/effects, Bosch brand colors only.
The governance model helps AI systems decide which source to prioritize: Brand Guide for visual style, BDDS for digital placement and UI constraints.
AI outputs should be evaluated not only visually but also by governance, accessibility, and legal constraints.
minimum_rules_an_ai_should_follow: Treat Bosch Brand Guide illustration style as the root visual authority.
Use BDDS when the output is a digital interface, software screen, or UI-supporting illustration.
Generate flat 2.5D geometric illustrations, not photorealistic renders or generic stock cartoons.
Use Bosch brand colors only, ideally one accent color scheme plus gray gradations.
Avoid gradients, glossy effects, reflections, heavy shadows, and arbitrary colors.
Represent people abstractly with brand colors or gray tones, not naturalistic skin colors.
Use centered foreground focus, supporting middle-ground elements, and reduced background context.
Avoid inserting critical readable text inside the image unless a text alternative is also planned.
Flag outputs for design review when they create new Bosch illustration assets.
prompt_engineering_implications_without_: Prompts should explicitly constrain geometry, color, depth, and effects.
Prompts should describe the role of each illustration element: main subject, supporting objects, reduced environment.
Prompts should specify whether the context is brand/marketing or UI/digital product because the usage context changes composition and size constraints.
Prompts should include negative constraints such as no gradients, no glossy rendering, no stock cartoon style, no photorealistic 3D render, and no non-Bosch colors.
Prompts should include accessibility-aware constraints when illustrations are used in UI contexts.
